ayahs.textEnglish: ONE who is minded to ask might ask about the suffering which [in the hereafter] is bound to befall
those who deny the truth. [Know, then, that] nothing can ward it off,
[since it will come] from God, unto whom there are many ways of ascent:

ayahs.textArabic: تَعْرُجُ الْمَلٰۤىِٕكَةُ وَالرُّوْحُ اِلَيْهِ فِيْ يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهٗ خَمْسِيْنَ اَلْفَ سَنَةٍۚ
ayahs.textLatin: Ta‘rujul-malā'ikatu war-rūḥu ilaihi fī yaumin kāna miqdāruhū khamsīna alfa sanah(tin).
ayahs.textEnglish: all the angels and all the inspiration [ever granted to man] ascend unto Him [daily,] in a day the length whereof is [like] fifty thousand years…
Therefore, [O believer,] endure all adversity with goodly patience:
behold, men look upon that [reckoning] as something far away –
but, We see it as near!
[It will take place] on a Day when the sky will be like molten lead,
and the mountains will be like tufts of wool,
and [when] no friend will ask about his friend,

ayahs.textArabic: يُبَصَّرُوْنَهُمْۗ يَوَدُّ الْمُجْرِمُ لَوْ يَفْتَدِيْ مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِىِٕذٍۢ بِبَنِيْهِۙ
ayahs.textLatin: Yubaṣṣarūnahum, yawaddul-mujrimu lau yaftadī  min ‘ażābi yaumi'iżim bibanīh(i).
ayahs.textEnglish: though they may be in one another's sight: [for,] everyone who was lost in sin will on that Day but desire to ransom himself from suffering at the price of his own children,
and of his spouse, and of his brother,
and of all the kinsfolk who ever sheltered him,

ayahs.textArabic: وَمَنْ فِى الْاَرْضِ جَمِيْعًاۙ ثُمَّ يُنْجِيْهِۙ
ayahs.textLatin: Wa man fil-arḍi jamī‘ā(n), ṡumma yunjīh(i).
ayahs.textEnglish: and of whoever [else] lives on earth, all of them - so that he could but save himself.
But nay! Verily, all [that awaits him] is a raging flame,
tearing away his skin!
It will claim all such as turn their backs [on what is right], and turn away [from the truth],
and amass [wealth] and thereupon withhold [it from their fellow-men].
VERILY, man is born with a restless disposition.
[As a rule,] whenever misfortune touches him, he is filled with self-pity;
and whenever good fortune comes to him, he selfishly withholds it [from others].
Not so, however, those who consciously turn towards God in prayer.
[and] who incessantly persevere in their prayer
and in whose possessions there is a due share, acknowledged [by them],
for such as ask [for help] and such as are deprived [of what is good in life];
and who accept as true the [coming of the] Day of Judgment;

ayahs.textArabic: وَالَّذِيْنَ هُمْ مِّنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّهِمْ مُّشْفِقُوْنَۚ
ayahs.textEnglish: and who stand in dread of their Sustainer's chastisement –
for, behold, of their Sustainer's chastisement none may ever feel [wholly] secure;
and who are mindful of their chastity,

ayahs.textArabic: اِلَّا عَلٰٓى اَزْوَاجِهِمْ اَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ اَيْمَانُهُمْ فَاِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُوْمِيْنَۚ
ayahs.textLatin: Illā ‘alā azwājihim au mā malakat aimānuhum fa innahum gairu malūmīn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: [not giving way to their desires] with any but their spouses - that is, those whom they rightfully possess [through wedlock] -: for then, behold, they are free of all blame,

ayahs.textArabic: فَمَنِ ابْتَغٰى وَرَاۤءَ ذٰلِكَ فَاُولٰۤىِٕكَ هُمُ الْعَادُوْنَۚ
ayahs.textLatin: Fa manibtagā warā'a żālika fa ulā'ika  humul-‘ādūn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: whereas such as seek to go beyond that [limit] are truly transgressors;
and who are faithful to their trusts and to their pledges:
and who stand firm whenever they bear witness;
and who guard their prayers [from all worldly intent].
These it is who in the gardens [of paradise] shall be honoured!
WHAT, THEN, is amiss with such as are bent on denying the truth, that they run about confusedly to and fro before thee,
[coming upon thee] from the right and from the left, in crowds?

ayahs.textArabic: اَيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ مِّنْهُمْ اَنْ يُّدْخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيْمٍۙ
ayahs.textLatin: Ayaṭma‘u kullumri'im minhum ay yudkhala jannata na‘īm(in).
ayahs.textEnglish: Does every one of them hope to enter [by this means] a garden of bliss?
Never! For, behold, We have created them out of something that they know [only too well]!

ayahs.textArabic: فَلَآ اُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ الْمَشٰرِقِ وَالْمَغٰرِبِ اِنَّا لَقٰدِرُوْنَۙ
ayahs.textLatin: Falā uqsimu birabbil-masyāriqi wal-magāribi  innā laqādirūn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: But nay! I call to witness [Our being] the Sustainer of all the points of sunrise and sunset: verily, well able are We

ayahs.textArabic: عَلٰٓى اَنْ نُّبَدِّلَ خَيْرًا مِّنْهُمْۙ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوْقِيْنَ
ayahs.textLatin: ‘Alā an nubaddila khairam minhum, wa mā naḥnu bimasbūqīn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: to replace them with [people] better than they are; for there is nothing to prevent Us [from doing what We will].

ayahs.textArabic: فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوْضُوْا وَيَلْعَبُوْا حَتّٰى يُلٰقُوْا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِيْ يُوْعَدُوْنَۙ
ayahs.textLatin: Fa żarhum yakhūḍū  wa yal‘abū ḥattā yulāqū yaumahumul-lażī yū‘adūn(a)
ayahs.textEnglish: Hence, leave them to indulge in idle talk and play [with words] until they face that [Judgment] Day of theirs which they have been promised –

ayahs.textArabic: يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُوْنَ مِنَ الْاَجْدَاثِ سِرَاعًا كَاَنَّهُمْ اِلٰى نُصُبٍ يُّوْفِضُوْنَۙ
ayahs.textLatin: Yauma yakhrujūna minal-ajdāṡi sirā‘an ka'annahum ilā nuṣubiy yūfiḍūn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: the Day when they shall come forth in haste from their graves, as if racing towards a goal-post,

ayahs.textArabic: خَاشِعَةً اَبْصَارُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ  ۗذٰلِكَ الْيَوْمُ الَّذِيْ كَانُوْا يُوْعَدُوْنَ ࣖ
ayahs.textLatin: Khāsyi‘atan abṣāruhum tarhaquhum żillah(tun), żālikal-yaumul-lażī kānū yū‘adūn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: with downcast eyes, with ignominy overwhelming them: that Day which they were promised again and…
